title: Compliance Snapshot Composer — per-tenant audit bundles for SOC 2 / ISO 27001
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a lightweight, tenant-aware snapshot composer that assembles time-bounded audit bundles for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 reviews. Each snapshot bundle should include a signed manifest, exported artifacts (logs, policy configs, access grants), redaction metadata, and a compact change-diff so auditors can verify what changed since the last snapshot. Bundles must respect data-residency constraints and retention settings, and should be exportable to ZIP or an S3/GCS export location.
acceptance_criteria: Console UI: user can request a snapshot for a tenant and pick time window (start/end) and target jurisdiction
Composer produces a ZIP bundle with a machine-readable manifest (JSON) and SHA256 checksums for all artifacts
Bundles include a signed manifest using Redwood KMS key material (customer-owned KMS optional)
Export respects tenant retention rules and automatically redacts or omits PII per tenant policies
Composer enforces residency: artifacts stored in region matching tenant policy or a manifest noting cross-region export with approvals
End-to-end pipeline processes a snapshot within 15 minutes for <1GB bundles and reports status in Console
API and CLI available: /v1/composer/snapshots POST and GET to download bundle or check status
Audit trail created: who requested snapshot, IP, and time; entries available in audit logs
implementation_plan: Design manifest schema and bundle layout (manifest.json, artifacts/, diffs/, signature.sig)
Extend existing evidence collectors to emit artifact metadata and last-modified hashes
Composer service: orchestrates collectors, applies redaction rules, packages artifacts, signs manifest
Storage layer: enforce region writes and temporary staging with retention TTL matching tenant policy
Console: simple flow for requesting, previewing, and downloading snapshots; include estimated size/time
API: create composer endpoints and webhook for completion/failure notifications
QA: run functional tests with sample tenants and mocked KMS, run performance tests on large tenant datasets
Rollout: gated beta with 3 customers, then gradual tenant opt-in
technical_notes: Prefer streaming zip creation to avoid full memory copies for large bundles
Use incremental collectors where possible: if last snapshot exists, only collect changed artifacts and include a diff manifest
Signature: use AWS KMS Encrypt/Sign APIs for hosted KMS; allow customer-provided KMS key ARN for Private deployments
Redaction: pipeline should support policy-driven redaction rules plus a manual metadata-only export mode for auditors
Residency: composer will verify artifact provenance and, if required, run collectors in the customer region (Dedicated/Private) or mark artifacts with cross-region consent
Cost considerations: large snapshot generation should be rate-limited and accounted separately (snapshot credits)
risks: Potential exposure of sensitive data if redaction rules incomplete — mitigated by manual review mode and post-generation scanning
KMS integration complexity across cloud providers and Private deployments — plan early integration tests
High CPU / IO for very large tenants causing service interference — implement concurrency limits and background priority queue
Auditor expectations vary; must offer flexible export formats and clear documentation
rollout_plan: Feature flag behind tenant-level beta flag
Initial beta with internal compliance team and two pilot customers (one NA, one EU) to validate residency behavior
Collect feedback, iterate on manifest shape and redaction UI
Open to larger cohort, monitor composer latency, failure rate, and support load
GA after 8 weeks if SLOs and compliance checks pass
test_plan: Unit tests for manifest generation and checksum verification
Integration tests with collectors producing artifacts across regions
End-to-end tests using a sample tenant with retention and redaction rules enabled
Security review and threat-modeling exercise before beta
Load test: generate 50 concurrent 2GB snapshots in staging to measure IO saturation
